newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-RIOS SHOWS TASTE FOR ADVERSITY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIOS SHOWS TASTE FOR ADVERSITY.

text.p: Marcelo Rios may look at times like he could not care less, as in his second successive five-setter at the French Open on Thursday when he came from two sets down to beat Byron Black of Zimbabwe.
In fact, the seventh seeded Chilean loves the challenge of taking on the world which, for the moment, is Roland Garros and a tough third round clash with local favourite Arnaud Boetsch on Saturday.

"I'm looking forward it, Boetsch on centre court, it's a difficult match with the crowd against me. I like that," Rios said after wriggling free to beat Black 6-7 6-7 6-4 7-6 6-0 as the sun was setting over Paris.
"It's fun to be against the world on a court and more fun if I win."
Rios said the experience of two successive five-set matches, coincidentally against brothers Wayne and Byron Black, stood him in good stead for the tournament.

"It was like playing the Davis Cup against Zimbabwe," the 21-year-old said with a grin. "Each match was different, but winning both like that gives me a lot of confidence. It proves that even if I'm losing I can win.
"I never think that I'm going to lose, but (Black) was playing really good."

Rios, the Monte Carlo champion, said it was the first time he had won after dropping the first two sets. He added that "I didn't expect to go to five sets in two days here, but that's good for the next match."
He said he was not playing as well as he had in winning at Monte Carlo in April and reaching the final of the Italian Open earlier this month.
"But I feel good physically and you can't always win playing well, but it's good if you can win playing badly."

Rios may find most of the Paris crowd against him when he plays Boetsch, but he enjoys avid support from a vociferous if small contingent of Chilean fans at Roland Garros, who were crestfallen after two sets but jubilant by the end.
